record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: LetS n be the set of permutations ofnordered by the strong Bruhat order. Characterize the intervals ofS n that are boolean algebras and compute their total number.

evidence.quote: [Stan2012, Ch. 3 Exer. 183(f)] LetS n be the set of permutations ofnordered by the strong Bruhat order. Characterize the intervals ofS n that are boolean algebras and compute their total number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, equipped with the strong Bruhat order $\le$, defined as the transitive closure of the relation $u \lessdot u t$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(ut) = \ell(u)+1$ (with $\ell$ the Coxeter length, i.e. the number of inversions). For $u \le v$ in $S_n$, the interval $[u,v]$ is the poset $\{w \in S_n : u \le w \le v\}$. A finite poset is called a Boolean algebra of rank $k$ if it is isomorphic to the poset $2^{[k]}$ of subsets of a $k$-element set ordered by inclusion.

(a) Give a characterization (for example, in terms of pattern avoidance, reduced-word data, or another combinatorial invariant) of those pairs $u \le v$ in $S_n$ for which the Bruhat interval $[u,v]$ is a Boolean algebra.

(b) Compute the total number of Boolean intervals in the Bruhat order on $S_n$, i.e.
$$ b(n) := \#\{(u,v) \in S_n \times S_n : u \le v \text{ and } [u,v] \text{ is a Boolean algebra}\}, $$
as an explicit function of $n$ (or by an explicit generating function).
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization of Boolean intervals in the Bruhat order on the symmetric group is known: an interval $[u,v]$ is Boolean iff a (any) reduced word for $vu^{-1}$-type data has no repeated letter, equivalently characterized via pattern avoidance (notably 321 and 3412 for principal Boolean ideals), as established in Tenner's "Pattern avoidance and the Bruhat order" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 2007), with enumeration formulas for the number of such intervals in $S_n$. Subsequent work has extended these characterizations to general intervals and other Coxeter-group settings.

status_evidence.title: Pattern avoidance and the Bruhat order (Tenner)
status_evidence.snippet: An element is boolean iff a reduced decomposition has no repeated letters; permutations with Boolean principal order ideals are exactly those avoiding 321 and 3412.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization and enumeration of Boolean (principal) Bruhat intervals in S_n is given via pattern avoidance and reduced-word criteria.

status_evidence.title: Interval structures in the Bruhat and weak orders
status_evidence.snippet: Pattern characterizations and enumerations for Boolean (and other) intervals in the symmetric group's Bruhat order.
status_evidence.claim: General Bruhat intervals that are Boolean lattices are characterized and enumerated for S_n.
